title: What do you do, where do you live
title_target: ເຮັດວຽກຫຍັງ ຢູ່ໃສ — Hét wîak nyǎng, yùu sǎi
goal: Say what you do for a living, ask about other people's jobs, say where you live and for how long — small talk that comes up faster in Laos than almost anywhere.
bekal: ask about someone's job with ເຮັດວຽກຫຍັງ
name your job with ເປັນ
ask ດົນບໍ່ and answer with a length of time
join two sentences with ແລະ and ແຕ່

dialogs.title: ບົດສົນທະນາ — At the coffee shop across from the office
dialogs.intro: Bounmy and Budi sit down for a moment before a meeting. Notice that not a single verb in this dialogue changes form — only the words around it change.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ບູດີ|Buu-dii] [ເຈົ້າ|jâo][ເຮັດ|hét][ວຽກ|wîak][ຫຍັງ|nyǎng]

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ເປັນ|pen][ວິສະວະກອນ|wi-sa-wa-kawn] [ເຮັດ|Hét][ວຽກ|wîak][ຢູ່|yùu][ບໍລິສັດ|baw-li-sát][ນ້ຳ|nâm]
lines.id: I'm an engineer. I work at the water company.
lines.literal: I — be — engineer. make — work — at — company — water.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ໂອ້|Ôo] [ດີ|dii][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai] [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ເປັນ|pen][ນັກ|nak][ບັນຊີ|ban-síi][ຢູ່|yùu][ນີ້|nîi][ຄື|khʉʉ][ກັນ|kan]
lines.id: Oh, great. I'm an accountant here too.
lines.literal: oh — good — much. I — be — expert — bookkeeping — at — here — same — together.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ເຈົ້າ|Jâo][ຢູ່|yùu][ບໍລິສັດ|baw-li-sát][ນີ້|nîi][ດົນ|dón][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Have you been at this company long?

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ສາມ|Sǎam][ປີ|pii][ແລ້ວ|lèeo] [ເຈົ້າ|Jâo][ເດ|dee] [ມາ|Maa][ລາວ|Láao][ດົນ|dón][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Three years now. What about you? Have you been in Laos long?
lines.literal: three — year — already. you — how-about? come — Laos — long — (question)?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ບໍ່|Bàw][ດົນ|dón] [ສອງ|Sǎwng][ອາທິດ|aa-thit][ເທົ່າ|thao][ນັ້ນ|nân]
lines.literal: not — long. two — week — only — that.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ເຈົ້າ|Jâo][ພັກ|phak][ຢູ່|yùu][ໃສ|sǎi]

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຢູ່|Yùu][ບ້ານ|bâan][ສີສະເກດ|Sǐi-sa-kèet] [ໃກ້|Kâi][ຕະຫຼາດ|ta-làat] [ຍ່າງ|Nyàang][ມາ|maa][ນີ້|nîi][ໄດ້|dâi]
lines.id: In Sisaket village, near the market. I can walk here.
lines.literal: at — village — Sisaket. near — market. walk — come — here — can.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ໃກ້|Kâi][ດີ|dii][ເນາະ|nāw] [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ຢູ່|yùu][ໄກ|kai] [ຂັບ|Khap][ລົດ|lot][ສາມ|sǎam][ສິບ|síp][ນາທີ|náa-thíi]
lines.id: Close by, nice. I'm far away — a thirty-minute drive.
lines.literal: near — good — isn't-it? I — be-at — far. steer — vehicle — three — ten — minute.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ບໍ່|Bàw][ໜັກ|nak][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai] [ແຕ່|Tèe][ຫຍຸ້ງ|nyûng][ຕອນ|tawn][ທ້າຍ|thâai][ເດືອນ|dʉan]
lines.id: Not too hard, but busy at the end of the month.
lines.literal: not — heavy — much. but — busy — part — end — month.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ເຂົ້າໃຈ|Khào-jai][ແລ້ວ|lèeo] [ໄປ|Pai][ປະຊຸມ|pa-sum][ກັນ|kan][ເນາະ|nāw]
lines.id: Got it. Let's go to the meeting.
lines.literal: enter-heart — already. go — meeting — together — okay?

notes: **ເຮັດວຽກ hét wîak is one package: "to work."** Literally "make work." To ask about someone's profession, Lao people say *ເຮັດວຽກຫຍັງ* (work what) — not *ເປັນຫຍັງ*, because *ເປັນຫຍັງ pen nyǎng* is already taken for "why."
**Answer with ເປັນ.** *ຂ້ອຍເປັນວິສະວະກອນ* (I'm an engineer). There's no word for "a/an"; Lao has no articles at all.

**ຢູ່ yùu does three jobs, and all of them appear in this dialogue.** (1) "to be at": *ຂ້ອຍຢູ່ວຽງຈັນ*. (2) "at/in" as a preposition: *ເຮັດວຽກຢູ່ບໍລິສັດ*. (3) an "ongoing" marker at the end of a sentence: *ລໍຖ້າຢູ່* (waiting). Context separates them, and you'll get used to it faster than you think.
**ດົນ dón means "long (time)."** *ດົນບໍ່* = "has it been long?" The answer: *ດົນແລ້ວ* (a long time) or *ບໍ່ດົນ* (not long). ⚠️ Don't use *ຍາວ nyáao* — that's "long" for objects, not for time.
**ແລ້ວ lèeo at the end means "already."** *ສາມປີແລ້ວ* = "three years already." It's the only past marker you need for now, and it goes **after** the verb phrase, not before it.
**ເທົ່ານັ້ນ thao nân = "only, just that much."** Used to play down an amount: *ສອງອາທິດເທົ່ານັ້ນ* (just two weeks). In fast speech it's often shortened to *ເທົ່ານັ້ນລະ*.
**ເນາະ nāw is the "isn't it?" particle.** It invites the listener to agree and makes you sound warm: *ໃກ້ດີເນາະ* (close by, nice, isn't it?). Use it for comments and opinions, not for real questions.

**ແຕ່ tèe = "but," ແລະ lae = "and."** In everyday speech *ແລະ* is often **dropped** and two sentences are simply placed side by side: *ຂ້ອຍເປັນນັກບັນຊີ ຂ້ອຍຢູ່ວຽງຈັນ*. The word *ແລະ* shows up more in writing.

**ເຂົ້າໃຈ khào-jai = "to understand," literally "enter the heart."** Lao builds dozens of feeling words with *ໃຈ jai* (heart): *ດີໃຈ dii-jai* (glad), *ເສຍໃຈ sǐa-jai* (sad), *ໃຈຮ້ອນ jai hâwn* (impatient, literally "hot heart"), *ໃຈເຢັນ jai yén* (patient, "cool heart").

grammars.title: Asking about places: ຢູ່ໃສ and friends
body: The question word *ໃສ sǎi* always stands **where the answer goes**, after the verb. Never at the start of the sentence.

after: ⚠️ *ໄປໃສມາ pai sǎi maa* (literally "go where come") is an everyday greeting meaning "where have you been?" — like "what are you up to?" in English: small talk, not an interrogation. Safe answers: *ໄປຕະຫຼາດມາ* (I've been to the market) or simply *ໄປຫຼິ້ນ pai lîn* (just out and about).

grammars.title: The verb never changes — the words around it do the work
body: This is Lao's biggest promise to beginners. The word *ໄປ pai* (to go) has exactly the same form in every sentence below.

after: Keep this table. These eight lines are the frame for almost every sentence you'll make in this course.

blocks.text: Notice the prefix **ນັກ *nak-*** — it means "expert, someone involved in," and attaches to the field: *ນັກຮຽນ* (one who studies), *ນັກຂ່າວ* (news person), *ນັກກິລາ nak-ki-láa* (athlete), *ນັກຮ້ອງ nak-hâwng* (singer). If you know the field, you can guess the job — much like English *-er* or *-ist*.

The pair **ພໍ່- / ແມ່-** is systematic too: literally "father" and "mother," but in front of a verb they mark a male/female doer. *ພໍ່ຄ້າ* male merchant, *ແມ່ຄ້າ* female merchant, *ແມ່ຄົວ mèe-khúa* cook.

Say it
English
Example
rows: *ສາມມື້ແລ້ວ* — three days now
*ສອງອາທິດ* — two weeks
*ຫົກເດືອນ* — six months
*ສາມປີແລ້ວ* — three years now
*ສອງຊົ່ວໂມງ* — two hours
*ສາມສິບນາທີ* — thirty minutes

blocks.text: ⚠️ Keep **ຊົ່ວໂມງ *sùa-móong*** (hours as a length: "two hours") apart from **ໂມງ *móong*** (o'clock: "two o'clock"). Mixing them up wrecks appointments, and it's a mistake people really do make.

What do you do?
I'm an engineer; I work at the water company.
Have you been in Laos long?
Not long, just two weeks.
I live near the market.
The work isn't too hard, but it's busy.

answers: ເປັນ — ເຮັດ — ຢູ່ — ຢູ່ — ແມ່ນ
ຂ້ອຍບໍ່ໄປຕະຫຼາດ — ຂ້ອຍໄປຕະຫຼາດແລ້ວ — ຂ້ອຍຊິໄປຕະຫຼາດ — ຂ້ອຍຢາກໄປຕະຫຼາດ — ຂ້ອຍໄປຕະຫຼາດບໍ່ໄດ້ — ໄປຕະຫຼາດບໍ່
ເຈົ້າເຮັດວຽກຫຍັງ — ເຈົ້າພັກຢູ່ໃສ — ສາມປີແລ້ວ — ເຈົ້າຢູ່ນີ້ດົນບໍ່ — ວຽກບໍ່ໜັກຫຼາຍ
ເຈົ້າເຮັດວຽກຫຍັງ — ຂ້ອຍເປັນວິສະວະກອນ ເຮັດວຽກຢູ່ບໍລິສັດນ້ຳ — ມາລາວດົນບໍ່ — ບໍ່ດົນ ສອງອາທິດເທົ່ານັ້ນ — ຂ້ອຍຢູ່ໃກ້ຕະຫຼາດ — ວຽກບໍ່ໜັກຫຼາຍ ແຕ່ຫຍຸ້ງ
